newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-BAYERN WAIT FOR KLINSMANN TO RE-DISCOVER HIS GOAL TOUCH.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BAYERN WAIT FOR KLINSMANN TO RE-DISCOVER HIS GOAL TOUCH.

text.p: Bayern Munich may have recaptured the lead in the Bundesliga with last week's 1-0 win over Karlsruhe, but striker Juergen Klinsmann's prolonged scoring drought is casting an ominous shadow over the team.
Hoping to bounce back from their early exit from the UEFA Cup in the first round, Bayern faces a daunting challenge on Saturday in a key match when they travel to Bremen.
It has been 17 years since Bayern last won in Bremen's Weser Stadium and the visitors will be hoping the struggling Klinsmann can spring back to life against seventh-place Werder.
Klinsmann has scored just two league goals in seven matches and has failed to find the net in the Bundesliga since August 25.

His sub-par performance has been dominating German media headlines for weeks and his failure to convert a penalty in Bayern's hollow 1-0 win over Valencia on Tuesday spawned a new outpouring of doubts about the 32-year-old captain of the German national team.
After losing 3-0 to Valencia in the first leg two weeks ago, Bayern relinquished their grip on the trophy and are now even more focused on regaining the league title.
Klinsmann, who bolted past the media on Tuesday night without taking any questions after missing the penalty, later said he was taking a lot of heat for the whole team's weak UEFA showing.

"It is no reason to go and stick my head in the sand," the he said of the missed penalty. "I don't see myself in a down phase. It is rather an attempt by some people to suggest I am having a crisis. There is no crisis. I just need a few goals."
In other matches, second-place Stuttgart will be aiming to rebound from their first defeat of the season last Saturday against Duesseldorf when they travel to play 1860 Munich.
If Bayern slip up in Bremen, Stuttgart will go top if they beat the southern city's rejuvenated second club.
Friday: Karlsruhe v Arminia Bielefeld; 1FC Cologne v Bochum

Saturday: Werder Bremen v Bayern Munich; 1860 Munich v VfB Stuttgart; SV Hamburg v MSV Duisburg; Schalke 04 v Bayer Leverkusen; Freiburg v Hansa Rostock; Fortuna Duesseldorf v Borussia Moenchengladbach.
Sunday: Bourssia Dortmund v St Pauli.
